# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a fat woman who waddles when she walks briskly. She sits habitually by her kitchen window watching the main road in Avonlea.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Lynde is a capable, energetic, and highly observant woman who manages her own affairs and keeps a sharp eye on those of her neighbors. Extremely outspoken and opinionated, she prides herself on always speaking her mind without hesitation. Although noted for her meddlesome curiosity, pessimistic warnings, and firm opinions on politics and upbringing, she possesses a very kind heart, readily helps the poor, and does not hold grudges once an apology is made.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P30](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0030), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c9 P10](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0010)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived with her meek husband, Thomas, in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road. She served as a prominent leader in community organizations, including the Sewing Circle, Sunday School, Church Aid Society, and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert decided to adopt a child, Rachel was astonished and openly doubted the wisdom of bringing an orphan into Green Gables. During her first visit to meet Anne Shirley, Rachel bluntly criticized the girl's looks, prompting Anne to burst into a furious temper, though Rachel readily forgave her when Anne apologized. Over the following years, Rachel frequently offered advice on Anne's upbringing and school affairs, eventually admitting she had been mistaken in her harsh initial judgment as Anne blossomed into a steady and capable girl. Following the death of her husband Thomas after a prolonged illness, Rachel faced financial difficulty due to an unpaid mortgage on her farm. Rather than move away to live with her daughter Eliza outside Avonlea, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables and share the house.

## Background by volume

- Has lived as a neighbor to Green Gables for forty-five years  <sub>[v2 c26 P17](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0017)</sub>
